title: RNA circularization preserves dynamics and enables in-cell relaxation NMR.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched the Zenodo record metadata (2 files, CC-BY-4.0, open). Downloaded and unzipped r1rho_analysis.zip (119,583 bytes): it holds 9 real files, all Python/config (r1_rho_fitting.py, r1_rho_equations.py, exponential_fitting.py, matrix_calculations.py, utility_functions.py, settings.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) plus Mac resource forks - zero data files. Read the ZIP central directory of 'Raw data Annecke Bekcic 2026.zip' (68,382,011 bytes) by a ranged HTTP request without downloading the body: 1,179 entries, all of them raw Bruker spectrometer acquisition folders (fid, acqus, acqu, pulseprogram, uxnmr.par, specpar) under sample directories such as 'HeLa_ch44-top rep 1' and 'rep 2', plus three TIFF gel images ('GU degradation gel.tif', 'GUG degradation gel.tif', 'miR degradation gel.tif'). No CSV, TSV, XLSX or any tabular file exists in either archive.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The construct list (GU, GUG, H44-top, MiR34a:Sirt1, each linear and circular, plus circGUGextended) and the only fitted exchange rates quoted in the text (kex,circ = 9339 and kex,lin = 14718 per second) come from the full text. Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 are referenced but Europe PMC's supplementary-file endpoint timed out, so the supplement was not retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record 20748774 is open with a CC-BY-4.0 licence; I downloaded one file in full and read the other's file listing. No login or application needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. Nothing in the deposit is a table. The quantities a model would predict (relaxation rates, exchange rate kex, excited-state population) exist only as numbers inside the paper's figures and text; to get them you would have to Fourier-transform raw Bruker FIDs (free induction decays, the instrument's raw time-domain signal), pick peaks, and run the authors' fitting scripts. That is constructing the label from scratch.

a3_inputs_present.note: RNA sequences for the handful of constructs are given in the methods and Supplementary Table S1, so inputs would be transcribable by hand - but only for about 9 sequences.

a4_units_stated.note: The paper states units clearly (rates in per second, concentrations in micromolar, pH values); not a failure point, but there is no units column because there is no table.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified. Four RNA hairpins (GU, GUG, H44-top, MiR34a:Sirt1) in linear and circular form plus one extended variant = 9 distinct RNA constructs, measured in 1-2 replicates. Even counting every imino proton in every construct as a row gives low hundreds at best, and they are not independent. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 68 MB of raw Bruker NMR directories plus three 1.4 MB TIFF gel images
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is trivially laptop-friendly; this is the only Part A item the dataset passes comfortably.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No count to disagree about: the deposit has no tables, and the number of sample directories is consistent with a study of ~9 constructs.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying measurements are genuine physical observations (nuclear magnetic resonance relaxation on real samples), not another model's output. A8 is not the problem here; A2 and A5 are.

existing_models.name: Dyna-1 (2026, published in Nature; predicts microsecond-to-millisecond protein dynamics from what is absent in deposited NMR spectra)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; found only as a search result, so no number is quoted here.

existing_models.name: RNA imino-group chemical shift predictor (Nature Communications 2021, PMC7952389; a lookup/semi-empirical model that predicts imino proton and nitrogen chemical shifts from the surrounding base-pair triplet, used to assign RNA excited states)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; listed because it shows the adjacent task is already modelled.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (an RNA language model) would be the natural backbone for RNA sequence input
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for 9 sequences, which is exactly the problem
backbone.licence: Not checked - irrelevant given the row count

integration.partner_dataset: BMRB (the Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank) holds deposited RNA chemical shifts and relaxation data
integration.join_key: RNA sequence or BMRB entry ID; this paper deposited nothing in BMRB, so there is no key in the files
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper's data: nine constructs add nothing joinable to a public resource.

controls.positive_control: None available at this scale - with 9 constructs there is no held-out set in which a known effect could be recovered.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless on 9 items.
controls.external_validation: BMRB holds RNA relaxation depositions, but this paper contributes no entries and no identifiers to join on.

honest_claim_h3: No honest machine-learning claim is possible from this deposit: it contains raw spectrometer output for nine RNA constructs and the fitting code, so any model would be fitting nine points.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an RNA hairpin's sequence to predict how fast it flickers between shapes, measured by magnetic resonance.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model would see: the RNA sequence (and whether the molecule is a closed circle or a linear hairpin). Verified count of distinct constructs in the deposit: 9.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the millisecond-timescale exchange rate and the fraction of molecules in the minor 'excited' shape, obtained by nuclear magnetic resonance relaxation dispersion - an experiment that detects fleeting alternative structures - then fitted with the authors' scripts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: RNA structural biologists would value a sequence-to-dynamics predictor because each measurement currently takes weeks of spectrometer time; but this paper supplies nine examples, which is three orders of magnitude short of what such a model needs.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict millisecond-timescale conformational exchange parameters (how fast an RNA flickers into a minor shape, and how much of it does) from RNA sequence plus a linear-versus-circular flag, with RNA-FM embeddings and a small regression head. Dies on sample size (9 constructs) and on the absence of any label table.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated beyond file sizes, because the project fails Part A before compute matters. Sizes are exact from the Zenodo API and the ZIP central directory.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct RNA constructs with a fitted exchange rate. I did this: 9. That single count kills it, and it took one text search.

verdict_reason: A high-quality biophysics methods paper, but not a machine-learning dataset. Two killers fail, both verified by opening the deposit rather than reading the paper. A2: the Zenodo record holds only raw Bruker spectrometer acquisition folders (1,179 entries, no CSV/TSV/XLSX anywhere) plus three gel photographs and a 119 KB folder of pure Python fitting code with no data in it - the prediction target would have to be built from raw time-domain signal by peak-picking and curve-fitting. A5: the study covers four RNA hairpins in linear and circular form plus one variant, nine constructs in total, against a checklist floor of ~1,500 rows. The data is open, small and CC-BY-4.0, and the fitting code is a genuinely useful release for NMR spectroscopists - it is just the wrong shape and scale for a model.
